judge_assessment.explanation: I re-derived every value the judge lists and all of them hold: sqrt(50)=7.0711 -> 7.07; sqrt(9)=3 > 2.9; sqrt(10)=3.1623 < 10/3=3.3333 < 3.5; sqrt(20)=4.4721 -> 4.47; sqrt(2)=1.4142 < 1.5; 27/5=5.4 < sqrt(30)=5.4772 < 5.5; pi=3.14159 < 22/7=3.142857; sqrt(85)=9.2195 -> 9.22; sqrt(45)=6.7082 > 6.7 > 20/3=6.6667; sqrt(18)=4.2426 < 17/4=4.25; 7/5=1.4 < 1.41 < sqrt(2)=1.41421 < 1.42; and -2.3 < -9/4=-2.25 < -sqrt(5)=-2.2361 < 2.4 < sqrt(6)=2.4495. The judge is right that rounding, squaring comparisons and negative ordering are handled correctly. What the judge did not check is the grading page and the response slots. Four of the twelve Quick Answers rows print nothing usable: '2. -', '5. -', '7. -' and '10. 4.25, -' - every one of them a relation that gate_log.txt records as PASS. On a worksheet whose declared facets are estimate-a-root, compare-two-quantities and order-a-list, a third of the answers are missing from the bank, and the sheet has no manual items at all, so the em-dash here reads as an outright gap rather than as 'see solution'. Two problems also print an uncovered slot: problem 1 asks 'Between which two consecutive whole numbers does sqrt(50) lie?' AND for the hundredth, and problem 4 asks for the hundredth AND 'name the two consecutive whole numbers it lies between' - verify.json holds only the approx entry for each, although curr-203 in this same run shows the fix (floor/ceiling eval entries). Problem 8's 'say which perfect square it is closer to, and why that tells you the answer is not half-way' and problem 12's 'sketch a number line and mark each one on it' are open-response and drawn slots with no manual entry.

strengths_to_preserve: The near-miss engineering across problems 7, 10 and 11 is the best thing on this sheet and it escalates deliberately: pi versus 22/7 agree to two decimals and separate at the third; sqrt(18) versus 17/4 differ by seven thousandths; problem 11 then puts 7/5, 1.41, sqrt(2), 1.42 inside a range of 0.02 and tells the student in the stem that 'two decimal places will not separate all of them - carry more'. A student cannot pass this sheet by rounding to two places out of habit.

Problem 5's stem teaches the method rather than only demanding the answer ('Squaring both is a quick way to be sure'), and the key follows through by squaring 1.5 to 2.25 and comparing with the radicand 2, so the technique the directions promise is the technique the key uses.

Problem 12 is a genuine synthesis rather than a longer version of problem 6: it mixes signs, so the rule stated in the directions ('on the negative side of zero the order reverses: the number furthest from zero is the least') is the only thing that gets -2.3 < -9/4 < -sqrt(5) right, and the ordering of the two negatives is the item most students lose.

Problem 10 is split into (a) convert 17/4 to a decimal and (b) then compare, which makes the comparison method explicit; verify.json backs part (a) with its own eval entry and declares the trap 'read the fraction bar as a decimal point' with value 17.4.

root_causes.description: The generated Quick Answers bank cannot print a relation. render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies string expecteds, sympify('<') raises, and the fallback prints '---'. On an ordering-and-comparing worksheet this removes a third of the bank's content, and because this sheet declares no manual items there is nothing else the glyph could mean - it simply looks like the author left four problems unanswered.
evidence: gate_log.txt records PASS for the compare entries of ids 2, 5, 7 and 10 (e.g. 'compare(sqrt(9) vs 2.9) -> > (expected >)').
answer_key.tex boxes the relations correctly in the worked solutions: 'sqrt(9) > 2.9', 'sqrt(2) < 1.5', 'pi < 22/7', 'sqrt(18) < 17/4' - so the bank disagrees with the same document two pages later.
verify.json contains no entry of type manual, and machine_observation.gate_chain_manual_flags = false.

root_causes.description: Compound stems were verified on their headline answer only. Problems 1 and 4 each ask for a bracketing pair as well as a hundredth, and problems 8 and 12 attach an explanation and a drawn number line to a numeric answer; only the numeric part is declared. The bracket case is the clearest, because curr-203 in this same run declares exactly those slots as floor/ceiling eval entries, so the capability exists and was simply not used here.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 1: 'Between which two consecutive whole numbers does sqrt(50) lie? ... then write sqrt(50) rounded to the nearest hundredth'; verify.json id 1 is a single approx entry.
worksheet.tex problem 4: 'Write sqrt(20) rounded to the nearest hundredth, and name the two consecutive whole numbers it lies between'; verify.json id 4 is a single approx entry.
curr-203/verify.json ids 1 and 2 declare floor(sqrt(n)) and ceiling(sqrt(n)) entries for the identical question shape.
worksheet.tex problem 8 ('Say which perfect square it is closer to, and why ...') and problem 12 ('then sketch a number line and mark each one on it') have no manual entry.

improvements.title: Render the four verified relations that currently blank out a third of this bank
improvements.proposed_change: Handle relation strings in render_quick_answers._fmt before the sympify attempt: for expected in {'<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!='}, print the operator between the entry's 'values' (id 2 -> 'sqrt(9) > 2.9'), and keep '---' only for ids whose entries are all manual. The formatter needs the whole entry rather than entry['expected'] alone so 'values' is available.
improvements.regression_test: Render this task's verify.json and assert that rows 2, 5, 7 and 10 all contain a relation operator and that no row equals '---'. Today four rows are em-dashes, so the assertion fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores four of twelve grading-bank answers on a sheet whose entire topic is comparison, and removes the false impression that the author left problems unanswered on a run with zero manual items.
improvements.risk: Relation rows are wider than bare numbers and can push the bank from four columns to three; column_count already adapts.

improvements.title: Declare the bracketing pairs in problems 1 and 4 the way curr-203 declares them
improvements.proposed_change: Enforce a response-slot inventory built from the worksheet stem: a stem that asks for a bracket AND a rounded value contributes two slots. Add floor(sqrt(n)) / ceiling(sqrt(n)) eval entries for ids 1 and 4 (n = 50 and 20), matching the pattern already used in curr-203/verify.json, and fail the build when a printed slot has no entry rather than reporting all gates green.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with problem 1's stem and a verify.json id 1 holding only {type: approx, expr: 'sqrt(50)', expected: 7.07}. The slot check must exit non-zero naming the uncovered bracketing slot; adding the floor and ceiling eval entries (7 and 8) makes it pass and makes the bank row read '7, 8, 7.07'.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes an inconsistency inside a single run - two tasks with the same question shape, one verified fully and one partially - and gives the grader the bracket that the key states in prose ('7 < sqrt(50) < 8', 'lying between 4 and 5') but nothing checks.
improvements.risk: More entries per problem lengthen bank rows; the id-to-row join already supports multiple entries, so the only cost is layout.

improvements.title: Flag problem 8's explanation and problem 12's number-line sketch as manual
improvements.proposed_change: Add the open-response verb and drawn-representation scan to the gate chain so a stem containing 'say which ... and why' or 'sketch a number line and mark each one on it' forces a manual entry on that id. Here that adds manual entries to ids 8 and 12 alongside their existing numeric checks.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with problem 12's stem ('Order these five values from least to greatest, then sketch a number line and mark each one on it') and a verify.json id 12 holding only the compare list. The check must exit non-zero naming the sketch slot; adding a manual entry makes it pass and the run exit code becomes 2.
improvements.expected_impact: The synthesis problem's drawn output - the thing that shows whether the student can place negatives on a line - stops being invisible to review on a sheet currently reported as having nothing to review.
improvements.risk: Two manual items on a twelve-problem sheet is a small review cost; the risk is verb-matching false positives on directions text, which scoping to the problem body mitigates.

case_summary: Twelve interleaved ordering problems whose mathematics is exact - I re-derived all thirteen checks including the three deliberate near misses (pi versus 22/7, sqrt(18) versus 17/4, and four values inside a 0.02 range) and found no error - with a genuinely escalating design and a synthesis item that forces the negative-ordering rule. The defects are on the grading page and in the coverage. Four of twelve Quick Answers rows print an em-dash for relations that the gate log records as PASS, on a sheet with no manual items at all, so a third of the bank is blank. Problems 1 and 4 each print a bracketing slot that verify.json does not cover, although curr-203 in this same run declares exactly that slot with floor/ceiling entries. Problem 8's 'and why' and problem 12's number-line sketch are open-response slots recorded as machine-verified. None of this touches the mathematics, so the ACCEPT stands.
